chunks: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God the Exalted: 'Does the human being not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?' He said: So he said: 'Neither measured nor configured.'

He said: And I asked him about His words: 'There surely came over the human being a period of time when he had not become a thing worthy of mention.' So he said: 'He was ordained without being mentioned.'

key_terms.الْبَدَاء: Bada' — the theological concept of God's 'alteration' of apparent divine decree, key Shia doctrine
key_terms.مَذْكُوراً: Worthy of mention (madhkur) — having a distinct, recognized identity in the cosmic record
key_terms.مُقَدَّراً: Measured/ordained (muqaddar) — referring to God's pre-eternal decree and measurement of a thing before it comes into existence
key_terms.مُكَوَّناً: Configured/constituted (mukawwan) — referring to actual formation and brought-into-existence state

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the pre-existence of humanity in Quran 19:67 and 76:1?
ai.summary: Malik al-Juhani asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about two Quranic verses relating to the pre-existence of human beings. The Imam clarified that regarding Quran 19:67, the human being at that stage was 'neither measured nor configured' — i.e., had no definite form or determined existence. Regarding Quran 76:1, he clarified that the human being 'was ordained without being mentioned' — meaning God had decreed its existence but it had not yet been given a distinct identity. This hadith is central to the Shia theological concept of Bada', illustrating the distinction between divine pre-measurement (taqdeer) and actual manifestation (takween).
